review.summary: Gorilla combines APIBench, AST-based API-call evaluation, and retrieval-aware fine-tuning of LLaMA to improve API selection and call generation across several model hubs. Reported results are strong on the evaluated tasks, while also revealing substantial dependence on retrieval quality and a narrower empirical scope than the paper’s broad API ambitions.

observations.claim: The paper presents a useful end-to-end benchmark and training setup for API-call generation, with a held-out evaluation.
observations.quote: We emphasize that we have maintained a holdout test set on which we report our findings.

observations.claim: On reported zero-shot results, Gorilla exceeds listed GPT baselines for all three hub datasets, though evaluation conventions differ by dataset.
The HuggingFace evaluation uses a weaker correctness check for comparison models than for Gorilla, limiting direct cross-model comparability there.
observations.quote: for all the models except Gorilla, we only check if they can provide the correct domain names.

observations.claim: Practical retrieval remains a significant bottleneck: the authors report large accuracy drops when substituting evaluated retrievers for the oracle.
observations.quote: using GPT-Index at evaluation results in 29.20% accuracy degradation, and using BM25 results in a 52.27% accuracy degradation.

unresolved_questions: How well do these results transfer to APIs outside the three hubs and to real user requests or executable multi-step tool workflows?
How representative and reproducible are the benchmark examples, generated instructions, and reported gains across API versions and stronger retrieval systems?
The inspected passages do not establish the robustness of adaptation to documentation changes beyond illustrated examples; what systematic test-time update evaluation was performed?
